**My thinking:**

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. We have about 6 mu of flat dryland. Everyone around me grows winter wheat followed by summer maize — that is what the soil knows, that is what the buyers want, that is what the government extension station teaches. I am not going to try something different. My husband does seasonal work in the city so I handle most of the field management myself, though my son helps during busy seasons.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it last October. Right now in April it is jointing. I already applied the base fertilizer at seeding. I still need to do one more nitrogen topdressing and one more irrigation before heading. Then I wait for June harvest. Right after the combine leaves I will direct-seed the maize into the stubble — no need to plow, saves money and time, and the village machine station operator does it quickly.

For seeds, I use the improved wheat variety my neighbor has used for three years — she gets 450 jin per mu, which is good. For maize I buy the hybrid from the county seed store, same one as last year. It costs more but the yield is worth it.

I put on fertilizer the way my family always has — a full bag of diammonium phosphate at planting, then urea top-dress at jointing. I know the extension station says to use less nitrogen but I worry about a low harvest. Maize gets a base plus one top-dress.

Water is expensive — I pay per hour of pump. I do 3 irrigations for the wheat total across the season and try to rely on summer rain for maize, but I will irrigate once if July is dry.
